items.excerpt: Sony Music has now asked platforms to remove more than 260,000 AI deepfake tracks imitating artists like Harry Styles, Adele and Michael Jackson, telling the FT the fight against soundalike AI tracks is 'becoming an uphill struggle'.

Joe Bonamassa says using Suno to write a lyric is 'not a high crime or misdemeanour' and sympathises with emerging artists using AI for an edge, but argues AI 'artists' shouldn't chart alongside humans.
Suno launches Albums: creators can group their AI-made songs into a full release, build an album draft (including from an existing playlist), organize track order and publish it on Suno.

MBW Explains: what the US appeals court's rejection of ROSS Intelligence's fair-use defense over AI training (Thomson Reuters v. ROSS) could mean for UMG and Sony's lawsuit against Suno. Note: follow-up angle on the ruling already covered 10/01.

Pope Leo XIV posts that it is 'urgent to distinguish human art from what machines produce', claiming an 'ontological difference' between art and statistically generated output; Music Ally frames it against the music industry's AI fight.
Follower and listener counts on Spotify's biggest editorial playlists are slipping, which a new report links to Spotify's crackdown on fake accounts and AI slop rather than waning interest.

'Make Me Metal' by Banoffee, an experimental track made with Suno v6, debuts with a music video directed by Emmy-winning choreographer Nina McNeely (separate artist from the already-covered Braylon Browner film in the same campaign).
Suno confirms its v6 model is trained in part on user-generated interactions, as new Sony/UMG copyright lawsuits land barely a week after the v6 launch.

Andrew Huang YouTube Short titled 'AI scammers are trying to use me', flagging AI-driven scams exploiting his name. Body unverified (Short has no description); the downstream enrichment pass should confirm the details.
